author: jadudm
message:
Moved code to JavaScript

I was doing a lot of work to do DB queries to populate web pages with template
variables. For example, on the start page, I wanted to look into the DB and
pre-load the fields if someone had already visited. This required a lot of work
in Python. The alternative: create a new endpoint in Flask that handles a JSON
request.

This approach lets me set id = "modelField" in my HTML for all of the text
fields. If the fields have the same id's as the names of the model fields, then
I can do a JSON request, get back an object, and walk the keys of that object.
These can automatically be turned into IDs on the webpage, and I can populate
the values of the form (if the values existed).

That may have made no sense. However, the end-result is less code on the server
(or, a simplified interface...), because now I've moved all form population
based on old data into a GET endpoint (or a POST... I should think about that),
and that endpoint does a query and simply JSONifies the object that is found.
That object is walked, and the values in the object directly stuffed into
fields.

Honest. It's easier.

author: jadudm
message:
Updated to handle new model, fixed start()

This involves some changes and learning as I updated the data model.

The model has more foreign key constraints now, and a linking table.

For example:

    facQ = (Faculty.select()
      .join(FacultyProjects, on = (FacultyProjects.fid == Faculty.fid))
      .join(Projects, on = (FacultyProjects.pid == Projects.pid))
      .where(Faculty.username == username)
      .where(FacultyProjects.corresponding == True)
      )

This is the join to pull out the faculty member if they are a corresponding
author on one project.

projectQ = (Projects.select()
        .join(Faculty, on = (theFaculty.fid == Projects.corresponding))
        )

pulls out all the projects which that faculty member is a corresponding member
for... and there should be only one. I'm not sure if we can enforce that,
except for making sure that one faculty member cannot insert more than one
project. Hm. That is probably not handled at the moment.

There's also a bunch of "session timeout" code that is almost entirely
untested, but is something that we should explore/discuss further. The session
(read: cookie) information is important, possibly, and I would like to make
sure I know how/why I'm using it. It isn't clear how it is valuable.

author: jadudm
message:
Starting to store and autofill data.

At this point, the code demonstrates a simple router, which serves
as a primary switch for the application. All functionality is broken
out into functions to handle the saving of data, and forms are
templated with autofill where appropriate.

One issue here is that we get the username, which is not necessarily
a unique identifier, but we trust the BNumber more. We probably have
to trust the username, because that is the authentication token. There
is no way to authenticate a BNumber... it's a bogus piece of information
that the user provides.

The alternative is that we take the username and look up the Bnumber...
but, at the end of the day, the thing the user gives us through
their authetication is a username... which is probably what we should
consider as a 'primary key.'

To be debated.
